title: [Web][Windows] Export writes a 0-byte project.binary into the .pck -> "Corrupted header in binary project.binary (not ECFG)"
body:
### Godot version

`4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf` — **standard** build (not .NET/mono), Windows x86_64

### System information

- Windows 10 (10.0.19042), x86_64
- Export templates: official `Godot_v4.7.2-stable_export_templates.tpz`
  (sha512 `ca4d71c4d7b81dfc15d1a98baa07534aa95b03fdda78a0075b06672e1648d2e5f40980c9adc28d23e1b92e732ee7bf3461997aa804af74ec2fcd7a93ccb84079`),
  installed at `%APPDATA%\Godot\export_templates\4.7.2.stable\` (`version.txt` and all `web_*.zip` present)
- Project: pure GDScript (no C#), Web preset with `variant/extensions_support=false`, `variant/thread_support=false`
- Disk space was not exhausted (≈ 20 GB free); the whole Web export is ~40 MB and the `.pck` is ~1 MB

### Issue description

Exporting to Web with the **Windows** editor produces a `.pck` whose `project.binary` entry is
**0 bytes** — it is the only zero-length entry among the 504 entries in the archive. The exported
build therefore never boots (black canvas, no game).

The **same project** exports Web successfully on Linux CI with the **same** Godot version, so this
looks Windows-editor-specific.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Minimal project (this is enough — I reproduced it with a 5-entry project, not just the real game):

   `project.godot`
   ```ini
   config_version=5

   [application]
   config/name="WebProbe"
   run/main_scene="res://main.tscn"
   config/features=PackedStringArray("4.7", "GL Compatibility")

   [rendering]
   renderer/rendering_method="gl_compatibility"
   renderer/rendering_method.mobile="gl_compatibility"
   ```
   plus `main.tscn` (a `Node2D` with a `Label`) and an `export_presets.cfg` containing a Web preset
   (`variant/extensions_support=false`, `variant/thread_support=false`).

2. ```bash
   godot --headless --path . --import
   mkdir -p out
   godot --headless --path . --export-release "Web" "out/index.html"
   ```

3. Inspect the produced `out/index.pck`.

### Expected

The `.pck` contains the compiled project settings as `project.binary`, starting with the `ECFG`
magic — exactly like a **Windows Desktop** export of the same project does
(`project.binary`: 2478 bytes, first bytes `45 43 46 47` = `ECFG`, 443 entries in the archive).

### Actual

`project.binary` is present in the pck directory, but its **size is 0**
(`offset 989152`, `size 0`; the pck directory is at `dir_offset 989264`, 504 entries in total).
The exported `index.wasm` is **byte-identical in size** to the template's `godot.wasm`
(39,514,754 bytes), i.e. the pck was neither embedded nor appended either.

Serving `out/` over plain HTTP and opening it in Chrome gives:

```
ERROR: Corrupted header in binary project.binary (not ECFG).
   at: _load_settings_binary (core/config/project_settings.cpp:918)
ERROR: Couldn't load file 'res://project.binary', error code 16.
   at: _load_settings_text_or_binary (core/config/project_settings.cpp:1004)
ERROR: Error: Couldn't load project data at path "/". Is the .pck file missing?
   at: setup (main/main.cpp:2130)
```

All requested resources return **HTTP 200** (`index.html`, `index.js`, `index.wasm`, **`index.pck`**,
icons), so this is not a hosting/404 problem. The canvas stays black; the game never starts.

### Evidence (pck format 4: the directory lives at `dir_offset`, near EOF)

```python
import struct
d = open("out/index.pck", "rb").read()
print(d[:4])                                                  # b'GDPC'
q = struct.unpack("<Q", d[0x20:0x28])[0]
print("dir_offset =", q)                                      # -> 989264
n, = struct.unpack("<I", d[q:q + 4]); q += 4
print("entries =", n)                                         # -> 504
for _ in range(n):
    ln, = struct.unpack("<I", d[q:q + 4]); q += 4
    name = d[q:q + ln].decode(); q += ln
    off, size = struct.unpack("<QQ", d[q:q + 16]); q += 16 + 16 + 4
    if "project" in name:
        print(name, "offset", off, "size", size)              # -> project.binary offset 989152 size 0
```

The same parser on a working **Windows Desktop** export of the same project prints
`project.binary  offset 849424  size 2478`, and its first four bytes are `ECFG`.

### Why this is probably not one of the existing reports

- **#27168 / #44363** — same error string, but the reported cause is a `.pck` **larger than 2.1 GB**
  (32-bit signed int overflow). My `.pck` is ~1 MB with a valid directory; only that one entry is empty.
- **#116391** — same error string class, reported when the disk was running out of space. Here the
  export exited 0 with no warnings and the filesystem had plenty of room.

So the distinguishing symptom is: a **small, otherwise well-formed pck** whose single
`project.binary` entry has size 0, produced by the **Windows** editor, not reproducible on Linux
with the same engine and templates.

### CI comparison (why this slipped through a green CI)

The project that hit this is public: <https://github.com/sax1234567/idol-anomaly-hunter>.
Its `export-web` job runs on `ubuntu-latest` with the standard editor and `include-templates: true`
and exports fine. Its self-check only verifies that `index.html`, `./*.wasm` and `./*.pck` **exist**
and that no `./*.tmp` is left — a **0-byte `project.binary` inside the pck is invisible** to that kind
of check. (I have since added a pck-content check to the project's own tooling; that does not change
anything on Godot's side.)

### Workaround

Build the Web export on Linux (e.g. via CI) instead of using the Windows editor.

### Notes

- I could only test `4.7.2.stable` locally, so I don't know whether this is a regression or in which
  version it started.
- The mixed mono/standard situation is not involved: the standard (non-.NET) editor was used
  exclusively, and the project contains no C# (the mono editor refuses Web export outright with the
  expected "use a non-C# editor" message).
- Every command and reading above was executed and captured locally; the generated artifacts were
  cleaned up afterwards.
